lemma_5.statement: For any finite-dimensional vector space V over Q_l and any linear operator T on V, T is semisimple on V if and only if T is semisimple, equivalently diagonalizable, on V tensor_Q_l Q_l_bar.
lemma_5.proof:
Proof. Let K=Q_l and L=Q_l_bar, and put W=V tensor_K L with T_L=T tensor id_L. If V=0 the assertion is vacuous, so assume V nonzero. We use the following criterion: for a finite-dimensional vector space U over a field F and a linear operator S on U, S is semisimple (equivalently, every S-stable subspace has an S-stable complement) if and only if the minimal polynomial m_S is square-free, i.e. is a product of distinct irreducible polynomials. Indeed, view U as an F[x]-module by x acting as S. Since F[x] is a PID, the simple F[x]-modules are F[x]/(p) with p irreducible. If U is semisimple, it is a finite direct sum of simple modules, and the minimal polynomial is the least common multiple of their annihilators, hence a product of distinct irreducible polynomials. Conversely, if m_S is square-free, say m_S=product p_j with distinct irreducibles p_j, then the Chinese remainder theorem gives F[x]/(m_S) isomorphic to the product of fields product F[x]/(p_j). The action of F[x] on U factors through this product of fields; using the idempotents of the product, U decomposes as a direct sum of vector spaces over those fields, hence is semisimple. This proves the criterion.

Next, scalar extension does not change the minimal polynomial. Let m_T be the minimal polynomial of T over K. The action map K[x]/(m_T) -> End_K(V), f mod m_T -> f(T), is injective by definition of m_T. The algebra K[x]/(m_T) is finite-dimensional over K. Tensoring with L preserves injectivity because L is a K-vector space and hence flat. Under the canonical identifications (K[x]/(m_T)) tensor_K L = L[x]/(m_T) and End_K(V) tensor_K L = End_L(W) (the latter can be checked by choosing a K-basis of V), we obtain an injective L-algebra map L[x]/(m_T) -> End_L(W) sending f mod m_T to f(T_L). Therefore the kernel of L[x] -> End_L(W), f -> f(T_L), is exactly the principal ideal (m_T), so m_{T_L}=m_T.

By the criterion, T is semisimple on V if and only if m_T is square-free in K[x]. Also T_L is semisimple on W if and only if m_{T_L}=m_T is square-free in L[x]. Because K and L have characteristic 0, square-freeness is equivalent to gcd(m,m')=1, and this condition is preserved and reflected by the field extension K subset L: if gcd(m_T,m_T')=1 in K[x], Bezout's identity in K[x] remains valid in L[x], so m_T is square-free in L[x]; conversely, if m_T were not square-free in K[x], some irreducible p in K[x] would satisfy p^2 dividing m_T, and the same divisibility holds in L[x], so m_T would not be square-free in L[x]. Hence T is semisimple on V if and only if T_L is semisimple on W.

Finally, L=Q_l_bar is algebraically closed, so semisimplicity of T_L is equivalent to diagonalizability. If T_L is diagonalizable, W is a direct sum of eigenspaces and m_{T_L} is a product of distinct linear factors, hence square-free; by the criterion T_L is semisimple. Conversely, if T_L is semisimple, the criterion gives that m_{T_L} is square-free in L[x]. Since L is algebraically closed, m_{T_L}=product_{lambda in Lambda}(x-lambda) with distinct lambda. The primary decomposition theorem, equivalently the Chinese remainder theorem applied to the pairwise coprime factors x-lambda, gives W=direct sum_{lambda in Lambda} ker(T_L-lambda id_W). This is a decomposition of W into eigenspaces, so T_L is diagonalizable.

Combining the equivalences proves that T is semisimple on V if and only if T_L is semisimple on W, and in the latter case this is equivalent to T_L being diagonalizable.

lemma_4.statement: For any finite-dimensional vector space V over a field and any invertible linear operator T on V, T is semisimple if and only if T^{-1} is semisimple; in particular, semisimplicity of arithmetic Frobenius on a cohomology group implies semisimplicity of geometric Frobenius.
lemma_4.proof:
Let k be a field, let V be a finite-dimensional k-vector space, and let T be an invertible linear operator on V. We use the standard criterion for semisimplicity of a single operator: V is a semisimple k[T]-module, equivalently the minimal polynomial m_T(x) of T is square-free in k[x], meaning it has no repeated irreducible factor. In characteristic zero, and in particular over Q_l, this is equivalent to diagonalizability after extension to an algebraic closure. If one uses the diagonalizable-over-algebraic-closure definition directly, the result is also immediate by choosing an eigenbasis after scalar extension and inverting the eigenvalues; the minimal-polynomial proof below gives the stronger statement in the semisimple-module sense.

If V=0, then T is the zero-dimensional operator and both T and T^{-1} are semisimple vacuously. Assume V is nonzero. Since T is invertible, m_T(0) is nonzero. Indeed, if m_T(0)=0, then x divides m_T(x), so m_T(x)=x q(x) for some q(x) in k[x] of strictly smaller degree. Evaluating at T gives T q(T)=0. Multiplying by T^{-1} yields q(T)=0, contradicting the minimality of m_T.

Write m_T(x)=a_d x^d+...+a_1 x+a_0 with a_0 nonzero and d=deg m_T. Define the reciprocal polynomial m_T^*(x)=x^d m_T(x^{-1})=a_0 x^d+a_1 x^{d-1}+...+a_d.

First, m_T^* annihilates T^{-1}. From m_T(T)=sum_{i=0}^d a_i T^i=0, multiply by T^{-d} to get sum_{i=0}^d a_i T^{i-d}=0. Reindexing with j=d-i gives sum_{j=0}^d a_{d-j} (T^{-1})^j=0, which is exactly m_T^*(T^{-1})=0. Hence the minimal polynomial m_{T^{-1}}(x) divides m_T^*(x).

Now suppose T is semisimple. Then m_T is square-free. Factor it into distinct monic irreducibles: m_T=f_1...f_s. Because m_T(0) is nonzero, each f_r(0) is nonzero. For each r, set n_r=deg f_r and f_r^*(x)=x^{n_r} f_r(x^{-1}). We claim each f_r^* is irreducible up to a nonzero scalar. If f_r^*=g h with nonconstant g,h in k[x], then f_r^*(0) is the leading coefficient of f_r, hence nonzero; therefore g(0) and h(0) are nonzero. Reversing the factorization expresses f_r as a nonzero scalar times g^* h^*, where g^* and h^* are nonconstant reciprocal polynomials, contradicting the irreducibility of f_r. Moreover, if f_r and f_t are distinct monic irreducibles, then f_r^* and f_t^* are not scalar multiples of one another; otherwise reversing would make f_r and f_t scalar multiples, hence equal since both are monic. Therefore m_T^*(x)=product_{r=1}^s f_r^*(x) is square-free in k[x], up to an overall nonzero scalar, which does not affect square-freeness.

Since m_{T^{-1}} divides the square-free polynomial m_T^*, it is itself square-free: any irreducible factor of a divisor of a square-free polynomial occurs with exponent at most one. Thus T^{-1} is semisimple.

For the converse, apply the implication just proved to S=T^{-1}. Since S is invertible and S^{-1}=T, semisimplicity of T^{-1} implies semisimplicity of T. Hence T is semisimple if and only if T^{-1} is semisimple.

Finally, let V=H^i_et(X over bar F_q, Q_l), a finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space. Let F_ar be arithmetic Frobenius and F_geo be geometric Frobenius. By definition F_geo=F_ar^{-1}, and F_ar is invertible. If F_ar is semisimple, the equivalence proved above with T=F_ar shows that F_geo is semisimple. Over Q_l, semisimplicity agrees with diagonalizability after tensoring with bar Q_l, so this gives the claimed implication for the cohomology groups in the conjecture.

lemma_8.statement: If V and W are finite-dimensional \mathbb Q_\ell-vector spaces with invertible linear operators T_V and T_W, and \alpha:V \to W is a \mathbb Q_\ell-linear isomorphism satisfying \alpha \circ T_V = T_W \circ \alpha, then T_V is semisimple if and only if T_W is semisimple.
lemma_8.proof:
Let \bar{V}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell, \bar{W}=W\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell, \bar{T}_V=T_V\otimes 1, \bar{T}_W=T_W\otimes 1, and \bar{\alpha}=\alpha\otimes 1. Since \alpha is a \mathbb Q_\ell-linear isomorphism, \bar{\alpha} is a \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell-linear isomorphism, with inverse \bar{\alpha}^{-1}=\alpha^{-1}\otimes 1. Tensoring the intertwining relation \alpha\circ T_V=T_W\circ \alpha with \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell gives \bar{\alpha}\circ \bar{T}_V=\bar{T}_W\circ \bar{\alpha}. Indeed, on an elementary tensor v\otimes c, the left-hand side sends v\otimes c to \alpha(T_Vv)\otimes c, while the right-hand side sends it to T_W(\alpha(v))\otimes c, and these are equal by the hypothesis. Hence \bar{T}_W=\bar{\alpha}\circ \bar{T}_V\circ \bar{\alpha}^{-1}.

Assume first that T_V is semisimple. By lemma_5, \bar{T}_V is diagonalizable on \bar{V}. Thus there exists a finite \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell-basis e_1,\dots,e_n of \bar{V} and scalars \lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n\in\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell such that \bar{T}_V(e_i)=\lambda_i e_i for every i. Set f_i=\bar{\alpha}(e_i). Because \bar{\alpha} is an isomorphism, f_1,\dots,f_n is a basis of \bar{W}. For each i,
\bar{T}_W(f_i)=\bar{\alpha}\circ \bar{T}_V\circ \bar{\alpha}^{-1}(f_i)=\bar{\alpha}\circ \bar{T}_V(e_i)=\lambda_i\bar{\alpha}(e_i)=\lambda_i f_i.
Thus \bar{T}_W has a basis of eigenvectors, so \bar{T}_W is diagonalizable. By lemma_5 again, T_W is semisimple.

Conversely, assume T_W is semisimple. By lemma_5, \bar{T}_W is diagonalizable on \bar{W}. Since \bar{T}_W=\bar{\alpha}\circ \bar{T}_V\circ \bar{\alpha}^{-1}, we also have \bar{T}_V=\bar{\alpha}^{-1}\circ \bar{T}_W\circ \bar{\alpha}. Let g_1,\dots,g_n be a basis of \bar{W} consisting of eigenvectors of \bar{T}_W, say \bar{T}_W(g_i)=\mu_i g_i. Then h_i=\bar{\alpha}^{-1}(g_i) form a basis of \bar{V}, and for each i,
\bar{T}_V(h_i)=\bar{\alpha}^{-1}\circ \bar{T}_W\circ \bar{\alpha}(h_i)=\bar{\alpha}^{-1}\circ \bar{T}_W(g_i)=\mu_i\bar{\alpha}^{-1}(g_i)=\mu_i h_i.
Therefore \bar{T}_V is diagonalizable. By lemma_5, T_V is semisimple.

Combining the two implications gives T_V semisimple if and only if T_W semisimple. The invertibility of T_V and T_W is not needed for the argument; the essential point is that the operators are conjugate by the isomorphism \alpha.

lemma_9.statement: Let V_1,\dots,V_m be finite-dimensional \mathbb Q_\ell-vector spaces and let T_j:V_j\to V_j be invertible \mathbb Q_\ell-linear operators. The direct-sum operator T=\bigoplus_{j=1}^m T_j on V=\bigoplus_{j=1}^m V_j is semisimple if and only if each T_j is semisimple.
lemma_9.proof:
Let K=\mathbb{Q}_\ell and k=\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell. For a K-vector space U and a K-linear operator S, write U_k=U\otimes_K k and S_k=S\otimes 1_k. The finite direct sum distributes over tensor product: there is a canonical k-linear isomorphism \Phi:(\bigoplus_{j=1}^m U_j)_k\to\bigoplus_{j=1}^m (U_j)_k, given by \Phi((u_j)\otimes a)=(u_j\otimes a)_j, and under this isomorphism (\bigoplus_j S_j)_k corresponds to \bigoplus_j (S_j)_k.
By lemma_5, for each finite-dimensional K-vector space U and K-linear operator S, S is semisimple on U if and only if S_k is diagonalizable on U_k. Applying this to U=\bigoplus_j V_j and S=T, and to each U=V_j and S=T_j, reduces the desired equivalence to the following claim over the algebraically closed field k: if W_1,\dots,W_m are finite-dimensional k-vector spaces and S_j:W_j\to W_j are k-linear operators, then S=\bigoplus_j S_j on W=\bigoplus_j W_j is diagonalizable if and only if each S_j is diagonalizable.
We prove the claim. The cases m=0 and zero-dimensional summands are vacuous, so when using minimal polynomials assume the relevant spaces are nonzero. First suppose each S_j is diagonalizable. For each j, choose a basis B_j of W_j consisting of eigenvectors of S_j (if W_j=0, take B_j empty). The union B=\bigsqcup_j B_j, viewed as vectors embedded in the corresponding summand of W, is a basis of W. For b\in B_j, S(b)=S_j(b)=\lambda b for some \lambda\in k. Hence B is a basis of eigenvectors of S, so S is diagonalizable.
Conversely, suppose S is diagonalizable. Each W_j is S-invariant under the natural inclusion W_j\hookrightarrow W. If W_j=0, S_j is diagonalizable by convention. Otherwise let m_S be the minimal polynomial of S. Since S is diagonalizable over k, m_S splits as a product of distinct linear factors, m_S(x)=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}(x-\lambda). For the restriction S|_{W_j}, the polynomial m_S annihilates it because m_S(S)w=0 for every w\in W_j. Therefore the minimal polynomial m_j of S|_{W_j} divides m_S. A divisor of a product of distinct linear factors is again a product of distinct linear factors. Over an algebraically closed field, an operator is diagonalizable if and only if its minimal polynomial is a product of distinct linear factors; indeed, if m_j(x)=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda_j}(x-\lambda), the primary decomposition gives W_j=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda_j}\ker(S|_{W_j}-\lambda I), an eigenspace decomposition. Thus S|_{W_j} is diagonalizable, i.e. S_j is diagonalizable. This proves the claim.
Returning to K, T is semisimple on V if and only if T_k is diagonalizable on V_k. Under the canonical isomorphism above, T_k corresponds to \bigoplus_j (T_j)_k. By the claim, this is diagonalizable if and only if each (T_j)_k is diagonalizable. By lemma_5 again, each (T_j)_k is diagonalizable if and only if T_j is semisimple on V_j. Hence T is semisimple if and only if each T_j is semisimple. The invertibility hypotheses are not needed for this equivalence.

lemma_3.statement: For a smooth projective variety X over F_q, there is a canonical isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces with arithmetic Frobenius action: Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_bar,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) ≅ H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l).
lemma_3.proof:
Let d = dim X and let X_bar = X x_{F_q} Spec(Fbar_q). Let D = D^b_c(X_bar, Q_l). Let F = F_arith: X_bar -> X_bar be the automorphism induced by x -> x^q on Fbar_q. The arithmetic Frobenius action on cohomology is the pullback action on RGamma(X_bar, Q_l). We prove that the analogous pullback action on Ext groups corresponds to it.

Step 1: Smooth case for IC_X. By the definition of the intersection complex, if X is smooth then IC_X is the shifted constant sheaf on X. With the Tate-twisted normalization there is a canonical isomorphism gamma: IC_X -> Q_l[d](d); with the untwisted normalization it is gamma: IC_X -> Q_l[d]. The proof below works for either normalization; if the Tate twist is present it cancels in the self-RHom.

Step 2: Computation of Ext groups. For each integer i, Ext^i_D(IC_X, IC_X) = Hom_D(IC_X, IC_X[i]). Conjugating by gamma gives a canonical isomorphism Hom_D(IC_X, IC_X[i]) -> Hom_D(L, L[i]), where L = Q_l[d](d) (or L = Q_l[d] in the untwisted normalization). Since [d] is an autoequivalence, Hom_D(L, L[i]) = Hom_D(Q_l(d), Q_l(d)[i]) (or Hom_D(Q_l, Q_l[i]) if untwisted). The sheaf-theoretic internal Hom of a rank-one Tate twist with itself is trivial: RHom_{X_bar}(Q_l(d), Q_l(d)) is canonically Q_l; similarly RHom_{X_bar}(Q_l, Q_l) is canonically Q_l. Therefore Hom_D(L, L[i]) = H^i(RHom_D(L,L)) = H^i(RGamma(X_bar, RHom_{X_bar}(L,L))) = H^i(RGamma(X_bar,Q_l)) = H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l). This gives a canonical Q_l-linear isomorphism Phi_i: Ext^i_D(IC_X,IC_X) -> H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l).

Step 3: Frobenius action on Ext. Since X is defined over F_q, IC_X carries its canonical Weil structure, i.e. a canonical isomorphism theta_F: F^*IC_X -> IC_X. For phi in Hom_D(IC_X, IC_X[i]), define F_Ext(phi) = theta_F[i] o F^*phi o theta_F^{-1}. This is a Q_l-linear automorphism of Ext^i_D(IC_X,IC_X), and it is the arithmetic Frobenius action on the Ext group.

Step 4: Compatibility with the cohomological Frobenius. The isomorphism gamma is compatible with the canonical Weil structures. If eta_F: F^*L -> L denotes the canonical descent datum on L = Q_l[d](d) (or on Q_l[d]), then eta_F o F^*gamma = gamma o theta_F. Hence, transported by gamma, the action F_Ext is the action on Hom_D(L,L[i]) given by psi -> eta_F[i] o F^*psi o eta_F^{-1}.

To identify this action, use the internal Hom. For L = Q_l[d](d), its dual is L^vee = RHom_{X_bar}(L,Q_l) = Q_l[-d](-d), and the canonical evaluation map L^vee tensor L -> Q_l is an isomorphism of Weil sheaves: the Weil structure on L^vee is the inverse of the Weil structure on L, so the tensor product has trivial Weil structure. Consequently the canonical isomorphism RHom_{X_bar}(L,L) -> Q_l is F-equivariant. Applying RGamma gives an F-equivariant isomorphism RHom_D(L,L) -> RGamma(X_bar,Q_l). Taking H^i identifies the action psi -> eta_F[i] o F^*psi o eta_F^{-1} with the action on H^i(RGamma(X_bar,Q_l)) induced by pullback along F on the constant sheaf Q_l. By definition, this is the arithmetic Frobenius action on H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l). In the untwisted normalization the same argument is immediate because L = Q_l[d] and RHom_{X_bar}(L,L) = Q_l with trivial Weil structure.

Thus for every phi in Ext^i_D(IC_X,IC_X), Phi_i(F_Ext(phi)) = F_H(Phi_i(phi)), where F_H is arithmetic Frobenius on cohomology. Hence Phi_i is an isomorphism in the category of Q_l-vector spaces equipped with a linear automorphism.

Step 5: Edge cases. If X is not connected, decompose it into finitely many connected components X_a. Then IC_X is the direct sum of the corresponding shifted constant sheaves on the components, and both Ext^i_D(IC_X,IC_X) and H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l) decompose as direct sums of the componentwise groups. Applying the above argument on each component gives the same canonical F-equivariant isomorphism. For i < 0 or i > 2 dim X the groups vanish, and the isomorphism is the zero isomorphism. The projectivity hypothesis is not needed for the identification itself, but it ensures finite-dimensionality.

Therefore there is a canonical isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces with arithmetic Frobenius action Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_bar,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) = H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l).

lemma_6a.statement: Let X be a scheme over F_q, let k = overline(F_q), and let sigma : k -> k be the q-power field automorphism sigma(a)=a^q. For every integer i >= 0 and every prime ell != p, the pullback maps F_ar := (id_X x sigma)^* and F_geo := (id_X x sigma^{-1})^* are Q_ell-linear automorphisms of H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell), and F_geo = F_ar^{-1}. In particular, if H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell, then the arithmetic and geometric Frobenius operators are invertible Q_ell-linear operators on it.
lemma_6a.proof: Fix an integer i >= 0 and a prime l != p. Let k = overline{F_q} and let sigma: k -> k be the q-power automorphism sigma(a)=a^q. Every element of F_q satisfies a^q=a, so sigma restricts to the identity on F_q; hence sigma is an F_q-automorphism of k, and sigma^{-1} is also an F_q-automorphism of k. Put X_k = X ×_{Spec F_q} Spec k. Define morphisms phi = id_X × sigma and psi = id_X × sigma^{-1} from X_k to X_k. Because products of morphisms over Spec F_q compose componentwise, phi ∘ psi = id_X × (sigma ∘ sigma^{-1}) = id_X × id_{Spec k} = id_{X_k}, and similarly psi ∘ phi = id_{X_k}. Thus phi and psi are inverse automorphisms of the scheme X_k. Étale cohomology with Q_l coefficients is a contravariant functor from schemes to graded Q_l-vector spaces. Therefore pullback along phi gives a Q_l-linear map F_ar := phi^*: H^i_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^i_et(X_k, Q_l), and pullback along psi gives a Q_l-linear map F_geo := psi^*: H^i_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^i_et(X_k, Q_l). The Q_l-linearity is part of the standard functoriality of Q_l-cohomology: pullback is linear on Z_l-cohomology and remains linear after forming Q_l-coefficients. For any composable morphisms f and g, functoriality gives (f ∘ g)^* = g^* ∘ f^*, and the identity morphism pulls back to the identity map. Applying this to f = phi and g = psi yields id = (phi ∘ psi)^* = psi^* ∘ phi^* = F_geo ∘ F_ar. Applying it to f = psi and g = phi yields id = (psi ∘ phi)^* = phi^* ∘ psi^* = F_ar ∘ F_geo. Hence F_ar and F_geo are mutual inverse linear maps on H^i_et(X_k, Q_l). In particular, each is a Q_l-linear automorphism of H^i_et(X_k, Q_l), and F_geo = F_ar^{-1}. No finiteness, smoothness, projectivity, or connectedness of X is needed for this formal argument; it also applies to the zero cohomology vector spaces if X_k is empty. If H^i_et(X_k, Q_l) is finite-dimensional over Q_l, then the preceding conclusion says precisely that arithmetic and geometric Frobenius are invertible Q_l-linear operators on that finite-dimensional vector space.

lemma_12.statement: For a smooth projective variety X over \mathbb F_q, the constant sheaf \mathbb Q_\ell on X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q}, equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure, is pure of weight 0.
lemma_12.proof:
Proof. We use the standard stalkwise definition of purity for a Frobenius sheaf on X_Fbar. Since the natural arithmetic Frobenius structure is descent data from X, purity is checked at closed points of X: a lisse Q_l-sheaf F with Frobenius structure is pure of weight w if for every closed point x of X, every geometric point bar x of X_Fbar lying over x, and every eigenvalue alpha of the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism Frob_x acting on the stalk F_{bar x}, one has |alpha| = q^{deg(x) w/2}, where deg(x) = [k(x):F_q] and |.| is taken via any embedding Q_l -> C. If the definition is formulated after extending scalars to Q_lbar, the same condition is obtained because scalar extension does not change the identity operator. If geometric Frobenius is used instead of arithmetic Frobenius, the conclusion is also the same here because the geometric action is the inverse of the arithmetic action, and in this lemma both are the identity.

Let F be the constant sheaf Q_l on X_Fbar, equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure. The sheaf F is lisse of rank 1. If X is empty, the purity condition is vacuous. Assume X is nonempty. Let x be a closed point of X, put d = deg(x) = [k(x):F_q], and choose a geometric point bar x of X_Fbar lying over x. The stalk of the constant sheaf at any geometric point is canonically Q_l, so F_{bar x} = Q_l.

The natural arithmetic Frobenius structure on the constant sheaf is the canonical descent isomorphism (id_X x sigma)^* Q_l -> Q_l, where sigma: Fbar -> Fbar is the q-power automorphism. Under the canonical identifications of the stalks of (id_X x sigma)^* Q_l and Q_l with Q_l, this descent isomorphism is the identity map on Q_l. Equivalently, the constant sheaf corresponds to the trivial Galois representation of Gal(Fbar/F_q), so arithmetic Frobenius acts trivially on every stalk. For a closed point x of degree d, the Frobenius automorphism Frob_x acting on the stalk is the d-fold iterate of this basic Frobenius structure; hence its action on F_{bar x} = Q_l is id_{Q_l}.

The matrix of id_{Q_l} on the one-dimensional Q_l-vector space Q_l is [1], so its only eigenvalue is 1. For weight 0, the required absolute value is q^{d * 0 / 2} = q^0 = 1, and |1| = 1. Therefore the stalkwise weight condition holds at x and bar x. Since x and bar x were arbitrary, F is pure of weight 0. Moreover, the Frobenius operator on each stalk is the identity, so it is semisimple and diagonalizable if such a condition is included in the definition of purity. The smooth projective hypothesis on X is not needed for this stalkwise verification.

lemma_11.statement: Let X be a smooth variety of pure dimension d over an algebraically closed field. The shifted constant sheaf \mathbb Q_\ell[d] is a perverse sheaf in D^b_c(X,\mathbb Q_\ell).
lemma_11.proof:
Proof. Let k be the algebraically closed field over which X is defined, and let a_X:X\to \operatorname{Spec} k be the structure morphism. We work in the usual étale six-functor formalism with coefficients \mathbb{Q}_\ell. The notation D^b_c(X,\mathbb{Q}_\ell) presupposes that \ell is invertible on X; since k is a field this means \operatorname{char}(k)\neq \ell. If X=\varnothing, then \mathbb{Q}_\ell[d]=0 and the zero complex satisfies the perverse support inequalities vacuously, so assume X is nonempty. Because X is smooth of pure dimension d, a_X is smooth of relative dimension d and \dim X=d.

Recall the perverse t-structure. For K\in D^b_c(X,\mathbb{Q}_\ell), put D_X(K)=\operatorname{RHom}(K,\omega_X), where \omega_X=a_X^!\mathbb{Q}_\ell is the \ell-adic dualizing complex. Then \mathcal{D}^{\le 0}(X) is the full subcategory of K such that \dim \operatorname{Supp} H^i(K)\le -i for every i, and \mathcal{D}^{\ge 0}(X) is the full subcategory of K such that \dim \operatorname{Supp} H^i(D_X(K))\le -i for every i. The heart \mathcal{D}^{\le 0}(X)\cap\mathcal{D}^{\ge 0}(X) is the category of perverse sheaves. The dimension of the empty support is taken to be -\infty.

First, K=\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d] lies in D^b_c(X,\mathbb{Q}_\ell). The constant sheaf \mathbb{Q}_\ell is locally constant of rank one, hence constructible, and shifting by a fixed integer preserves boundedness and constructibility.

Support condition. For every integer i,
H^i(\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d])\cong H^{i+d}(\mathbb{Q}_\ell).
Since \mathbb{Q}_\ell is a sheaf placed in cohomological degree 0, H^j(\mathbb{Q}_\ell) is \mathbb{Q}_\ell for j=0 and 0 otherwise. Therefore H^i(\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d]) is \mathbb{Q}_\ell for i=-d and 0 for i\neq -d. The support of \mathbb{Q}_\ell is X, whose dimension is d, and the support of the zero sheaf is empty. Hence \dim \operatorname{Supp} H^i(\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d])\le -i for all i: for i=-d we have d\le d, and for all other i the support is empty. Thus \mathbb{Q}_\ell[d]\in \mathcal{D}^{\le 0}(X).

Cosupport condition. We need the dual of K. Two facts are used.

1. Formal shift of Verdier dual. For any L\in D^b_c(X,\mathbb{Q}_\ell) and any integer n,
D_X(L[n])=\operatorname{RHom}(L[n],\omega_X)\cong \operatorname{RHom}(L,\omega_X)[-n]=D_X(L)[-n].
This is just the standard compatibility of internal Hom with shifts in the derived category.

2. Smooth duality. We invoke the standard smooth duality (cohomological purity) theorem for étale \ell-adic sheaves: if f:Y\to \operatorname{Spec} k is smooth of relative dimension n and \ell is invertible on Y, then
D_Y(\mathbb{Q}_\ell)=f^!\mathbb{Q}_\ell\cong \mathbb{Q}_\ell(n)[2n].
A reference is SGA 4½, Exp. 1, Théorème 1.1; the passage from finite torsion coefficients to \mathbb{Q}_\ell is the usual limit argument. The hypotheses are satisfied for f=a_X: k is algebraically closed, X is a variety of finite type, a_X is smooth of relative dimension d, and \ell is invertible on X. The theorem is a sheaf-level statement; no assertion that a smooth variety is étale-locally an open subscheme of affine space is needed.

Applying smooth duality to a_X gives D_X(\mathbb{Q}_\ell)\cong \mathbb{Q}_\ell(d)[2d]. Hence
D_X(\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d])\cong D_X(\mathbb{Q}_\ell)[-d]\cong \mathbb{Q}_\ell(d)[d].

Now compute cohomology sheaves. For every i,
H^i(D_X(\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d]))\cong H^i(\mathbb{Q}_\ell(d)[d])\cong H^{i+d}(\mathbb{Q}_\ell(d)).
The sheaf \mathbb{Q}_\ell(d) is a Tate twist of the constant sheaf; over an algebraically closed field its stalk at every geometric point is nonzero, so its support is X. Thus H^i(D_X(\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d])) is \mathbb{Q}_\ell(d) for i=-d and 0 otherwise. Consequently \dim \operatorname{Supp} H^i(D_X(\mathbb{Q}_\ell[d]))\le -i for all i: for i=-d the dimension is d=-(-d), and otherwise the support is empty. Thus \mathbb{Q}_\ell[d]\in \mathcal{D}^{\ge 0}(X).

Since \mathbb{Q}_\ell[d] belongs to both \mathcal{D}^{\le 0}(X) and \mathcal{D}^{\ge 0}(X), it is perverse. This completes the proof.

lemma_7.statement: Let X be a proper variety over F_q and let K be an object of D^b_c(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q}, \mathbb Q_\ell) equipped with an arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism \varphi:F_X^*K \xrightarrow{\sim} K. For every n, the vector space Ext^n_{D^b_c(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q}, \mathbb Q_\ell)}(K,K) is finite-dimensional over \mathbb Q_\ell, and \varphi induces a canonical arithmetic Frobenius automorphism on this Ext group.
lemma_7.proof:
Proof. Let Xbar = X times_{F_q} Fbar_q and let D = D^b_c(Xbar,Q_l). Let F_X be the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of Xbar over F_q, induced by x -> x^q on Fbar_q. This is an automorphism of the etale topos over F_q; it is not Fbar_q-linear. Hence pullback F_X^* is a Q_l-linear autoequivalence of D, with quasi-inverse pullback along the inverse automorphism. All Hom groups below are taken in D.

1. Finite-dimensionality. Put C = RHom(K,K). By the standard stability theorem for bounded constructible complexes, D is closed under derived internal Hom; since K is bounded constructible, C is bounded constructible. Thus each cohomology sheaf H^q(C) is constructible, and H^q(C) = 0 for all but finitely many q.

For every integer n,
Ext^n(K,K) = Hom(K,K[n]) ~= Hom(Q_l,RHom(K,K[n])) ~= Hom(Q_l,RHom(K,K)[n]) = Hom(Q_l,C[n]) = H^n(Xbar,C).
The first adjunction is Hom(A,B) ~= Hom(Q_l,RHom(A,B)) with A = K and B = K[n], and the second uses RHom(K,K[n]) ~= RHom(K,K)[n]. The last equality is the definition of etale hypercohomology.

Since C is bounded, the hypercohomology spectral sequence
E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Xbar,H^q(C)) => H^{p+q}(Xbar,C)
converges. Let I be the finite interval of q for which H^q(C) may be nonzero. For fixed n, the only possible E_2 terms with total degree n are E_2^{n-q,q} with q in I, so there are finitely many. Properness of X over F_q implies properness of Xbar over Fbar_q. The etale finiteness theorem for proper varieties over a separably closed field implies that each H^p(Xbar,H^q(C)) is finite-dimensional over Q_l. Hence the E_2 terms with p+q=n are finite-dimensional, and the E_infty terms with p+q=n are finite-dimensional subquotients of the corresponding E_2 terms. The abutment H^n(Xbar,C) has a finite filtration whose graded pieces are these E_infty terms. A finite extension of finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces is finite-dimensional. Therefore Ext^n(K,K) is finite-dimensional. No vanishing of Ext^n outside the cohomological interval of C is asserted; boundedness of C is used only to make the spectral sequence have finitely many terms in each fixed total degree. The empty variety is included, since all cohomology groups vanish.

2. Frobenius action. The given isomorphism phi: F_X^*K -> K induces an isomorphism theta: F_X^*C -> C. Since F_X^* is a symmetric monoidal autoequivalence, there is a canonical isomorphism
alpha: F_X^*RHom(K,K) -> RHom(F_X^*K,F_X^*K).
Because phi is an isomorphism, conjugation by phi gives an isomorphism
beta = RHom(phi^{-1},phi): RHom(F_X^*K,F_X^*K) -> RHom(K,K).
On morphisms, beta sends v: F_X^*K -> F_X^*K[m] to phi[m] o v o phi^{-1}: K -> K[m]. Define theta = beta o alpha.

Use the canonical identification F_X^*Q_l ~= Q_l. For a in H^n(Xbar,C) = Hom(Q_l,C[n]), define
Phi_n(a) = theta[n] o F_X^*(a),
where F_X^*(a) is regarded as a morphism Q_l -> F_X^*C[n] via F_X^*Q_l ~= Q_l. This is a Q_l-linear automorphism: it is the composition of the isomorphism Hom(Q_l,C[n]) -> Hom(F_X^*Q_l,F_X^*C[n]) induced by F_X^*, the identification Hom(F_X^*Q_l,F_X^*C[n]) ~= Hom(Q_l,F_X^*C[n]), and postcomposition with theta[n].

Finally, under the identification Ext^n(K,K) ~= H^n(Xbar,C), Phi_n corresponds to the automorphism
u -> phi[n] o F_X^*(u) o phi^{-1}
of Hom(K,K[n]). Indeed, if a_u: Q_l -> C[n] is the adjoint of u: K -> K[n], then F_X^*(a_u) has adjoint F_X^*(u): F_X^*K -> F_X^*K[n], and postcomposition with theta = RHom(phi^{-1},phi) conjugates this adjoint by phi. This is the canonical arithmetic Frobenius automorphism induced by phi. QED.

lemma_13.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q with connected components X_1,...,X_m. For every i >= 0, the restrictions to the components give a canonical isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces H^i_et(X_{Fbar_q}, Q_l) = direct sum_{j=1}^m H^i_et(X_{j,Fbar_q}, Q_l), and this isomorphism is equivariant for arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^q.
lemma_13.proof:
Let k be an algebraic closure of F_q, put Y = X_k, and put Y_j = (X_j)_k for each connected component X_j of X. If X is empty, both sides are zero; assume m >= 1.

Since X is of finite type over a field, it is Noetherian. A Noetherian topological space has finitely many irreducible components. Each connected component is a union of irreducible components, so X has finitely many connected components. Connected components are closed in any topological space; because there are only finitely many, the complement of any one is a finite union of closed sets, hence closed, so each X_j is also open. Thus X is the finite disjoint union of the open and closed subschemes X_j.

Base change preserves finite coproducts, so Y = X times_{F_q} k is the finite disjoint union of the open and closed subschemes Y_j = X_j times_{F_q} k. Let i_j: Y_j -> Y be the corresponding open and closed immersions. (The Y_j need not be connected; they are just the base changes of the components of X.)

For any sheaf F of Q_l-vector spaces on Y, the restriction functor F -> (i_j^*F)_{j=1}^m is an equivalence Sh(Y) isomorphic to product_{j=1}^m Sh(Y_j). To see this explicitly, if U -> Y is etale, then U decomposes uniquely as the disjoint union of the open and closed subschemes U_j = U times_Y Y_j, and a section of F over U is exactly a tuple of sections of F|_{U_j} over U_j. The inverse equivalence sends a tuple (F_j) to the sheaf U -> product_j F_j(U_j), which, since m is finite, is also the direct sum of the sheaves i_{j,*}F_j. Because i_j is open and closed, i_{j,*}=i_{j,!} is exact.

Apply this to the constant sheaf Q_l on Y. Its restriction to Y_j is the constant sheaf Q_l on Y_j, so the constant sheaf on Y corresponds to the tuple of constant sheaves on the Y_j. Hence, after viewing the Y_j as open and closed subschemes of Y, there is a canonical decomposition of sheaves Q_{l,Y} isomorphic to direct sum_j i_{j,*}Q_{l,Y_j}.

Under the equivalence Sh(Y) isomorphic to product_j Sh(Y_j), the global sections functor Gamma(Y,-) corresponds to the product of the global sections functors Gamma(Y_j,-). To compute the derived functors, take injective resolutions I_j^bullet of Q_{l,Y_j} in Sh(Y_j); the tuple (I_j^bullet) is an injective resolution of the tuple corresponding to Q_{l,Y}. Applying Gamma(Y,-) gives the complex product_j Gamma(Y_j,I_j^bullet). Since m is finite, this product is the direct sum of the complexes Gamma(Y_j,I_j^bullet), and finite direct sums are exact in Q_l-vector spaces. Taking cohomology therefore gives, for every i >= 0, a canonical isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces
H^i_et(Y,Q_l) isomorphic to direct sum_{j=1}^m H^i_et(Y_j,Q_l).
(If Q_l-cohomology is defined as H^i_et(-,Z_l) tensor Q_l, the same statement follows because finite direct sums commute with tensor products.)
By construction, this isomorphism is the map sending a cohomology class to the tuple of its restrictions i_j^*.

It remains to prove equivariance for arithmetic Frobenius. Let sigma: k -> k be sigma(a)=a^q. By Lemma 6a, the arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(Y,Q_l) is F_ar = (id_X times sigma)^*. Put f = id_X times sigma: Y -> Y. Since f is the identity on the X-factor, it preserves each open and closed subscheme X_j, and therefore it restricts to an automorphism f_j = id_{X_j} times sigma: Y_j -> Y_j. Again by Lemma 6a, f_j^* is the arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(Y_j,Q_l).

For each j, the square with vertical arrows f_j and f and horizontal arrows i_j commutes, and it is cartesian because f^{-1}(Y_j)=Y_j. Functoriality of inverse image sheaves gives a canonical identification i_j^{-1} f^{-1} isomorphic to f_j^{-1} i_j^{-1}. One can check this stalkwise: for a geometric point y of Y_j, the stalk of i_j^{-1} f^{-1}F is F_{f(y)}, and the stalk of f_j^{-1} i_j^{-1}F is (i_j^{-1}F)_{f_j(y)} = F_{f(y)}. Passing to derived global sections, this identification yields
i_j^* o f^* = f_j^* o i_j^*: H^i_et(Y,Q_l) -> H^i_et(Y_j,Q_l).
Thus each component of the restriction map commutes with arithmetic Frobenius. Consequently, if phi denotes the canonical isomorphism above, then
phi o F_ar = (direct sum_{j=1}^m F_ar,j) o phi,
where F_ar,j is arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^q on the j-th summand. This proves the lemma.

lemma_17.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q. The intersection complex IC_X on X_{Fbar_q} is an object of D^b_c(X_{Fbar_q}, Q_l) equipped with a canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure. Consequently, for every integer i, Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_{Fbar_q}, Q_l)}(IC_X, IC_X) is finite-dimensional over Q_l, and the induced arithmetic Frobenius map is a Q_l-linear automorphism.
lemma_17.proof:
Let k=Fbar_q and let σ:k→k be σ(a)=a^q. Let F_X=(id_X×σ)^* denote arithmetic Frobenius pullback on X_k. Since X is projective, X is proper. Write X=⊔_{r=1}^m X_r as the finite disjoint union of its connected components. Because X is Noetherian, this decomposition is finite and each X_r is open and closed in X; hence X_r is smooth projective over F_q. A smooth morphism to a field has locally constant relative dimension, and X_r is connected, so X_r is pure of some dimension d_r. Put Y_r=(X_r)_k. Then X_k=⊔_{r=1}^m Y_r, and each Y_r is smooth of pure dimension d_r over k. If X is empty, take m=0 and all assertions are trivial.

For each connected component Z of Y_r, Z is smooth, connected, and of dimension d_r. By the definition of the intersection complex, IC_Z is the intermediate extension of the shifted constant sheaf Q_l[d_r] from the smooth locus. Since Z is smooth, the smooth locus is all of Z, so this intermediate extension is canonically Q_l[d_r]. Lemma_11 says Q_l[d_r] is a perverse sheaf in D^b_c(Z,Q_l), so it is the normalized perverse sheaf IC_Z. Taking the direct sum over the finitely many connected components of Y_r gives a canonical isomorphism IC_{Y_r}≅Q_l[d_r]. Hence IC_X=⊕_{r=1}^m IC_{Y_r}≅⊕_{r=1}^m Q_l[d_r]. Lemma_11 and the fact that finite direct sums preserve D^b_c show that IC_X is an object of D^b_c(X_k,Q_l).

Lemma_12, applied to each smooth projective component X_r, supplies the constant sheaf Q_l on Y_r with a canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure; explicitly, it gives a canonical isomorphism φ_r^0:F_X^*Q_l→Q_l compatible with arithmetic Frobenius. Pullback commutes with cohomological shifts, so we obtain a canonical isomorphism φ_r^0[d_r]:F_X^*Q_l[d_r]≅(F_X^*Q_l)[d_r]→Q_l[d_r]. Let ψ_r:IC_{Y_r}→Q_l[d_r] be the canonical isomorphism above. Define
φ_r=ψ_r^{-1}∘(φ_r^0[d_r])∘F_X^*(ψ_r):F_X^*IC_{Y_r}→IC_{Y_r}.
This is a canonical arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism on IC_{Y_r}.

Since F_X preserves each Y_r (because Y_r=(X_r)_k and F_X=id_X×σ), and pullback is additive and commutes with finite direct sums, we have
F_X^*IC_X≅F_X^*(⊕_{r=1}^m IC_{Y_r})≅⊕_{r=1}^m F_X^*IC_{Y_r}.
Let ψ=⊕_{r=1}^m ψ_r. Combining the φ_r gives a canonical isomorphism
φ:F_X^*IC_X→IC_X.
Thus IC_X is an object of D^b_c(X_k,Q_l) equipped with a canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure.

Finally apply Lemma_7 to the proper variety X over F_q and to K=IC_X with the arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism φ. Lemma_7 states that for every integer n, Ext^n_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) is finite-dimensional over Q_l and that φ induces a canonical arithmetic Frobenius automorphism on this Ext group. Taking n=i yields the desired conclusion for every integer i. Concretely, the induced map sends a morphism u:IC_X→IC_X[i] to φ∘F_X^*(u)∘φ^{-1}; since F_X is an automorphism of X_k and φ is an isomorphism, this is a Q_l-linear automorphism.

lemma_18.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q and let l != p be prime. Suppose that for every n >= 0, arithmetic Frobenius acts semisimply on the finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space Ext^n_{D^b_c(X_{overline{F}_q},Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X). Then for every i >= 0, geometric Frobenius acts semisimply on H^i_et(X_{overline{F}_q},Q_l), and equivalently on H^i_et(X_{overline{F}_q},Q_l) tensor_{Q_l} Q_l_bar.
lemma_18.proof: Proof. Fix an integer i >= 0. Set V = Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_bar,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) and W = H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l). By hypothesis, arithmetic Frobenius T_V on V is a semisimple Q_l-linear operator on a finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space. Lemma 17 gives that the canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure on IC_X induces an automorphism on Ext^i(IC_X,IC_X); hence T_V is invertible. Lemma 3 gives a canonical Q_l-linear isomorphism phi_i: V -> W which is equivariant for arithmetic Frobenius, i.e. phi_i o T_V = T_W o phi_i, where T_W denotes arithmetic Frobenius on W. Since phi_i is an isomorphism and V is finite-dimensional, W is finite-dimensional. Lemma 6a gives that T_W is a Q_l-linear automorphism of W and that geometric Frobenius F_geo on W satisfies F_geo = T_W^{-1}. Applying Lemma 8 to the equivariant isomorphism phi_i and the invertible operators T_V and T_W, we conclude that T_W is semisimple on W. Applying Lemma 4 to the invertible operator T_W, we conclude that T_W^{-1} = F_geo is semisimple on W. Finally, Lemma 5 applied to W and the operator F_geo gives that F_geo is semisimple, equivalently diagonalizable, on W tensor_{Q_l} Q_l_bar = H^i_et(X_bar,Q_l) tensor_{Q_l} Q_l_bar. If W = 0, the same conclusions are trivial (and the above finite-dimensional and invertibility statements remain valid for the zero space). Since i was arbitrary, the statement holds for every i >= 0.

lemma_19.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q. With its canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure, the intersection complex IC_X on X_{Fbar_q} is a pure perverse sheaf of weight 0.
lemma_19.proof:
Let k = Fbar_q. If X is empty, then IC_X = 0, and the zero perverse sheaf is pure of weight 0 by the usual convention. Assume X is nonempty. Write X as a finite disjoint union of its connected components over F_q, X = union_j X_j. Each X_j is open and closed in X, hence smooth projective over F_q. Since a smooth morphism has locally constant relative dimension and X_j is connected, X_j has a pure dimension d_j. The canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure on IC_X is the direct sum of the canonical arithmetic Frobenius structures on IC_{X_j}. Therefore it suffices to prove the assertion for each X_j and then use the fact that finite direct sums of pure perverse sheaves of the same weight are pure of that weight.

Fix j and put Y = X_j. Over k, Y_k is smooth of pure dimension d_j. For a smooth pure-dimensional variety, the intersection complex is defined as the middle extension from the smooth locus of the constant local system Q_l shifted by the dimension. Here the smooth locus is all of Y_k, so the middle extension is just the shifted constant sheaf Q_l[d_j]. Thus there is a canonical Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism IC_Y = Q_l[d_j]. By lemma_11, Q_l[d_j] is a perverse sheaf. The canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure on IC_Y is the one induced by the natural arithmetic Frobenius structure on the constant sheaf Q_l; under the above identification it is exactly the natural arithmetic Frobenius structure on Q_l[d_j]. By lemma_12, Q_l with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure is pure of weight 0. In the normalized definition of weights for perverse sheaves, a lisse sheaf L pure of weight w on a smooth d-dimensional variety gives the perverse sheaf L[d] pure of weight w; equivalently, the shift by d is the perverse normalization and does not change the perverse weight. Applying this with L = Q_l, w = 0, and d = d_j, we obtain that Q_l[d_j] is a pure perverse sheaf of weight 0. Hence IC_Y is pure perverse of weight 0.

Finally, the direct sum step is legitimate because the weight filtration of a finite direct sum is the direct sum of the weight filtrations, and the subquotients of the direct sum are direct sums of the subquotients of the summands. Thus a finite direct sum of pure perverse sheaves of weight 0 is again pure of weight 0, and the canonical Frobenius structure is compatible with this decomposition. Consequently IC_X is a pure perverse sheaf of weight 0 for every smooth projective variety X over F_q.

lemma_16_frob_stable.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a proper variety over \mathbb{F}_q, let k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q, and let \ell \neq p be prime. Let K and L be objects of D^b_c(X_k,\mathbb{Q}_\ell) equipped with arithmetic Frobenius isomorphisms \varphi_K:F_X^*K \xrightarrow{\sim} K and \varphi_L:F_X^*L \xrightarrow{\sim} L, where F_X is the q-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism on X_k. Then for every integer i, the \mathbb{Q}_\ell-vector space Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_k,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)}(K,L) is finite-dimensional.
lemma_16_frob_stable.proof:
Let k = overline(F_q) and put M = K ⊕ L. Since D^b_c(X_k, Q_ℓ) is closed under finite direct sums, M is an object of D^b_c(X_k, Q_ℓ). The pullback functor F_X^* is additive, hence it preserves finite biproducts; therefore there is a canonical isomorphism F_X^*(K ⊕ L) ≅ F_X^*K ⊕ F_X^*L. Define φ_M : F_X^*M → M to be the composite F_X^*(K ⊕ L) ≅ F_X^*K ⊕ F_X^*L → K ⊕ L, where the second map is φ_K ⊕ φ_L. This is an arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism on M.

Because X is proper over F_q and M is an object of D^b_c(X_k, Q_ℓ) equipped with the arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism φ_M, Lemma lemma_7 applies to M. Hence for every integer i the Q_ℓ-vector space Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_k, Q_ℓ)}(M,M) is finite-dimensional.

Now use additivity of Ext in the Q_ℓ-linear triangulated category D^b_c(X_k, Q_ℓ). By definition Ext^i(A,B) = Hom_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_ℓ)}(A, B[i]). Since the shift functor [i] and Hom are additive, for any objects A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2 one has a natural isomorphism Hom(A_1 ⊕ A_2, B_1[i] ⊕ B_2[i]) ≅ Hom(A_1,B_1[i]) ⊕ Hom(A_1,B_2[i]) ⊕ Hom(A_2,B_1[i]) ⊕ Hom(A_2,B_2[i]). Equivalently, Ext^i(A_1 ⊕ A_2, B_1 ⊕ B_2) ≅ Ext^i(A_1,B_1) ⊕ Ext^i(A_1,B_2) ⊕ Ext^i(A_2,B_1) ⊕ Ext^i(A_2,B_2). Applying this with A_1=B_1=K and A_2=B_2=L gives a canonical Q_ℓ-vector-space isomorphism Ext^i(M,M) ≅ Ext^i(K,K) ⊕ Ext^i(K,L) ⊕ Ext^i(L,K) ⊕ Ext^i(L,L).

Let V = Ext^i(M,M) and W = Ext^i(K,L). The preceding decomposition identifies W as a direct summand of V: there are Q_ℓ-linear maps j: W → V and p: V → W with p ∘ j = id_W. Since V is finite-dimensional by the application of Lemma lemma_7, the subspace j(W) of V is finite-dimensional; because j is injective, W is finite-dimensional. Equivalently, W is the image p(V) of a linear map from a finite-dimensional space, hence finite-dimensional.

Therefore Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_k, Q_ℓ)}(K,L) is finite-dimensional for every integer i. If i lies outside the possible range of Ext, the group is zero, which is finite-dimensional, and the same argument covers this case.

lemma_1.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, and let X_1,...,X_r be its connected components over F_q. On X_bar = X over the algebraic closure of F_q, the intersection complex IC_X is a semisimple perverse sheaf, and there is a canonical isomorphism IC_X isomorphic to the direct sum over C in pi_0(X_bar) of Q_l[dim C]. For each i, the summand supported on the geometric connected components of (X_i)_bar is pure and semisimple, and the natural arithmetic Frobenius structure permutes these summands according to its action on pi_0(X_bar). Consequently IC_X is a finite direct sum of pure semisimple perverse sheaves; in particular, if X is pure-dimensional (equivalently, all geometric connected components have the same dimension; for example if X is connected), then IC_X itself is pure semisimple.
lemma_1.proof:
Let k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q and \bar X=X\times_{\mathbb F_q}k. Write IC_{\bar X} for the intersection complex of \bar X, i.e. the base change of IC_X. If \bar X=\varnothing all statements are vacuous, so assume it is nonempty. Let F=F_{\bar X}:\bar X\to\bar X be the arithmetic Frobenius morphism, induced by a\mapsto a^q on k. It is an automorphism and acts on \pi_0(\bar X) by C\mapsto F(C).

1. Canonical decomposition of IC.
For C\in\pi_0(\bar X), let j_C:C\hookrightarrow\bar X and let d_C=\dim C. Since C is open and closed, j_{C,*}=j_{C,!}; put S_C=j_{C,*}\mathbb Q_\ell[d_C].
The scheme \bar X is a finite disjoint union of its connected components. For a finite disjoint union of open and closed subschemes, the derived category and the perverse t-structure decompose as a direct sum, and the intersection complex is compatible with this decomposition. Hence IC_{\bar X} is the direct sum of the extensions by zero of the IC_C. It remains to identify IC_C.
The component C is smooth over k and connected. Smoothness over a field implies regularity. A regular Noetherian local ring is a domain, so C is locally irreducible; in a locally Noetherian scheme the irreducible components are open, and connectedness therefore implies that C is irreducible. Thus C is an irreducible smooth k-variety of pure dimension d_C. For an irreducible smooth variety, the intersection complex is the middle extension of the constant local system on the smooth locus. Since the smooth locus is all of C, this middle extension is \mathbb Q_\ell[d_C]. Therefore IC_C\cong\mathbb Q_\ell[d_C], and extending by zero gives a canonical isomorphism
IC_{\bar X}\cong\bigoplus_{C\in\pi_0(\bar X)}S_C=\bigoplus_{C\in\pi_0(\bar X)}\mathbb Q_\ell[\dim C].

2. Simplicity and semisimplicity.
By lemma_11, \mathbb Q_\ell[d_C] is perverse on C; since C is open and closed, S_C is perverse on \bar X. We claim S_C is simple. We use the standard simplicity theorem for middle extensions: if Y is irreducible, U\subset Y is dense open, and L is an irreducible local system on U, then j_{!*}L[\dim Y] is simple in Perv(Y). This theorem follows from the defining no-subobject and no-quotient-on-boundary properties of j_{!*}. Apply it first with coefficients \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell. The hypotheses hold: C is irreducible, and the constant local system \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell is irreducible because it is rank one over a field. Here U=C and j=\mathrm{id}, so \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell[d_C] is simple.
To descend to \mathbb Q_\ell, suppose A\hookrightarrow\mathbb Q_\ell[d_C] were a nonzero proper subobject in Perv(C,\mathbb Q_\ell). Scalar extension \mathbb Q_\ell\to\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell is exact, faithful, and t-exact on perverse sheaves. Hence A\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell is a nonzero proper subobject of \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell[d_C], contradiction. Thus \mathbb Q_\ell[d_C] is simple over \mathbb Q_\ell. The equivalence between Perv(C) and perverse sheaves on \bar X supported on C transfers simplicity to S_C.
If C\neq D, the supports of S_C and S_D are disjoint, so Hom(S_C,S_D)=0; in particular the S_C are pairwise non-isomorphic simple objects. Therefore IC_{\bar X}=\bigoplus_C S_C is a finite direct sum of simple perverse sheaves, hence semisimple.

3. Frobenius structure and permutation of summands.
Because X is defined over \mathbb F_q, the constant sheaf and the intersection complex carry their canonical arithmetic Weil structures. We use the convention \varphi:F^*IC_{\bar X}\to IC_{\bar X} for the standard arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism. For any sheaf G, Supp(F^*G)=F^{-1}(Supp G). Since F is a homeomorphism preserving dimensions, there is a canonical isomorphism
F^*S_C\cong S_{F^{-1}(C)}.
The natural isomorphism on constant sheaves gives \varphi(F^*S_C)=S_{F^{-1}(C)}. Equivalently, the inverse structure \psi=\varphi^{-1}:IC_{\bar X}\to F^*IC_{\bar X} sends the summand S_C to the summand F^*S_{F(C)}. Thus, with the convention that the Frobenius structure is written as an isomorphism from the object to its pullback, it permutes the labels C by the action C\mapsto F(C) of arithmetic Frobenius on \pi_0(\bar X); with the convention \varphi:F^*IC\to IC the induced permutation is the inverse C\mapsto F^{-1}(C). This fixes the convention and the support computation.
Let X_i be a connected component of X over \mathbb F_q and let \bar X_i=(X_i)_k. Since X_i is open and closed in X and defined over \mathbb F_q, F(\bar X_i)=\bar X_i; hence F permutes \pi_0(\bar X_i). Put
K_i=\bigoplus_{C\in\pi_0(\bar X_i)}S_C.
This is the summand of IC_{\bar X} supported on the geometric connected components of \bar X_i, and it is stable under the Frobenius structure.

4. Purity and semisimplicity of K_i.
The component X_i is smooth and projective over \mathbb F_q: it is open and closed in X, hence smooth, and closed in the projective scheme X, hence projective. It is connected, and by the argument above it is irreducible. Let d_i=\dim X_i. The smooth morphism X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb F_q has constant relative dimension d_i; after base change to k, every connected component C of \bar X_i is open and closed and smooth of pure dimension d_i. Hence
K_i=j_{i,*}\mathbb Q_\ell[d_i],
where j_i:\bar X_i\hookrightarrow\bar X is the clopen inclusion.
Lemma_12 says that the constant sheaf \mathbb Q_\ell on a smooth projective variety over \mathbb F_q, with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure, is pure of weight 0. Applying this to X, the complex \mathbb Q_\ell[d_i] on \bar X is pure of weight d_i. The inclusion j_i is clopen and Frobenius-stable, so K_i is a Frobenius-stable direct summand of this pure object. A Frobenius-stable direct summand of a pure object is pure, because its eigenvalues are among those of the ambient object. Therefore K_i is pure of weight d_i. It is semisimple because it is a direct sum of the simple objects S_C. Thus each K_i is a pure semisimple perverse sheaf.
Since \bar X=\bigsqcup_i\bar X_i, we have
IC_{\bar X}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r K_i,
a finite direct sum of pure semisimple perverse sheaves.

5. Pure-dimensional case.
For a smooth finite type scheme over a field, connected components are irreducible. Hence X is pure-dimensional in the usual sense, meaning all irreducible components have the same dimension, if and only if the integers d_i=\dim X_i are all equal. By the dimension statement above, for each i all geometric connected components of \bar X_i have dimension d_i. Therefore X is pure-dimensional if and only if all geometric connected components C\in\pi_0(\bar X) have the same dimension. If X is connected, then r=1, so this condition is automatic.
If all d_i are equal to d, then IC_{\bar X}=\bigoplus_i K_i is a direct sum of pure objects of the same weight d, hence is pure of weight d; it is semisimple by Step 2. Equivalently, IC_{\bar X}=\mathbb Q_\ell[d] on \bar X, and lemma_12 plus shifting gives purity. Thus, in the pure-dimensional case, IC_{\bar X} itself is pure semisimple.
This proves the lemma.

lemma_22.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, let l != p, and let IC_X be the intersection complex on X_bar. For every integer n >= 0, arithmetic Frobenius acts semisimply on the finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space Ext^n_{D^b_c(X_bar,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) if and only if arithmetic Frobenius acts semisimply on H^n_et(X_bar,Q_l).
lemma_22.proof: Fix an integer n >= 0. Write X_bar = X_{overline F_q}, V = Ext^n_{D^b_c(X_bar, Q_l)}(IC_X, IC_X), and W = H^n_et(X_bar, Q_l). Let T_V denote the arithmetic Frobenius operator on V induced by the canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure on IC_X, and let T_W denote the arithmetic Frobenius operator on W. By lemma_17, V is finite-dimensional over Q_l and T_V is a Q_l-linear automorphism. By lemma_6a, T_W is a Q_l-linear automorphism of W. By lemma_3, there is a canonical Q_l-linear isomorphism alpha: V -> W which is equivariant for the arithmetic Frobenius action; explicitly, alpha(T_V(v)) = T_W(alpha(v)) for every v in V. Since V is finite-dimensional and alpha is a vector-space isomorphism, W is finite-dimensional over Q_l. Hence alpha is an isomorphism of finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces intertwining the invertible operators T_V and T_W. Applying lemma_8, T_V is semisimple on V if and only if T_W is semisimple on W. This is exactly the assertion for the fixed n. Since n was arbitrary, the equivalence holds for every n >= 0. If the lemma is read in the global form, namely that arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on all Ext^n if and only if it is semisimple on all H^n, the same pointwise equivalence immediately implies both directions.

lemma_20.statement: Let X be a proper variety over \mathbb{F}_q and let K be a finite direct sum of simple perverse sheaves on X_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q} with coefficients in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell, equipped with an arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism \varphi:F_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K. Then there is a finite decomposition K=\bigoplus_{\alpha=1}^r K_\alpha such that each K_\alpha is the sum of the isotypic components of K lying in one orbit of the induced action of \varphi on the isomorphism classes of simple constituents, and \varphi(F_X^*K_\alpha)=K_\alpha. For every integer n, this gives a \varphi-equivariant direct-sum decomposition \operatorname{Ext}^n_{D^b_c(X_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q},\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)}(K,K)=\bigoplus_{\alpha,\beta=1}^r \operatorname{Ext}^n_{D^b_c(X_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q},\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)}(K_\alpha,K_\beta) of finite-dimensional \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell-vector spaces. Consequently, the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism induced by \varphi is semisimple on the left-hand side if and only if it is semisimple on every summand on the right-hand side.
lemma_20.proof: Let Xbar = X_{Fbar_q}, let F = F_X be the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of Xbar, and let Qbar_l denote an algebraic closure of Q_l. Put D = D^b_c(Xbar, Qbar_l) and P = Perv(Xbar, Qbar_l). If K = 0, take r = 0 and all statements are vacuous; assume K is nonzero. 1. Isotypic decomposition. Since K is a finite direct sum of simple objects of P, K is semisimple in the abelian category P. Let Sigma be the finite set of isomorphism classes of simple perverse sheaves occurring as constituents of K. For each class s in Sigma, let K_s be the sum of all simple subobjects of K whose class is s (equivalently, group any fixed finite direct-sum decomposition of K by isomorphism classes). Then K = direct sum_{s in Sigma} K_s. The morphism F is an automorphism of Xbar. Pullback F^* is an exact autoequivalence of D and of P: it is an equivalence of the etale topoi, and the perverse t-structure is defined by support and cosupport dimension conditions, which are invariant under a homeomorphism. Hence F^* sends simple perverse sheaves to simple perverse sheaves. Because K and F^*K lie in the heart P, the given isomorphism phi: F^*K -> K in D is an isomorphism in P, since Hom_D(A,B) = Hom_P(A,B) for A,B in the heart. For every simple constituent S of K, F^*S is a simple constituent of F^*K, and phi(F^*S) is a simple constituent of K. Thus sigma([S]) = [phi(F^*S)] = [F^*S] is a well-defined permutation of Sigma. It is bijective because F^* has an inverse autoequivalence. Let O_1,...,O_r be the orbits of sigma on the finite set Sigma. Define K_alpha = direct sum_{s in O_alpha} K_s. This gives the required finite decomposition K = direct sum_{alpha=1}^r K_alpha. We show phi(F^*K_alpha) = K_alpha. The object F^*K_alpha is a subobject of F^*K whose simple constituents have classes in O_alpha, because sigma preserves each orbit. Its image under the isomorphism phi is a subobject of K with the same composition factors, hence all its simple constituents lie in O_alpha. By semisimplicity, any such subobject is contained in K_alpha. The lengths of F^*K_alpha and K_alpha are equal because F^* is an autoequivalence of P. Therefore the inclusion phi(F^*K_alpha) subset K_alpha is an equality. Consequently phi restricts to an arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism phi_alpha: F^*K_alpha -> K_alpha. 2. Decomposition of Ext groups. For every integer n, finite direct sums are biproducts in the additive category D. Hence Ext^n_D(K,K) = Hom_D(K, K[n]) = direct sum_{alpha,beta=1}^r Hom_D(K_alpha, K_beta[n]) = direct sum_{alpha,beta=1}^r Ext^n_D(K_alpha,K_beta). This decomposition is canonical. The vector spaces Ext^n_D(K_alpha,K_beta) are finite-dimensional over Qbar_l. Indeed, K_alpha and K_beta are constructible complexes on the proper variety Xbar. The standard finiteness theorem for Ext between constructible complexes on a proper variety gives finite-dimensionality. In the notation of the available lemmas, this is the Qbar_l-coefficient form of lemma_16_frob_stable: lemma_16_frob_stable is stated for Q_l coefficients; for Qbar_l coefficients one either works in the scalar-extension category D^b_c(Xbar,Q_l) tensor_Q_l Qbar_l, or chooses a finite extension E/Q_l over which the finitely many objects and morphisms are defined, applies lemma_16_frob_stable to the corresponding underlying Q_l-objects, and extends scalars to Qbar_l. In either formulation, Ext^n_D(K_alpha,K_beta) is a finite-dimensional Qbar_l-vector space. Thus the whole Ext group is finite-dimensional. 3. Frobenius preserves the summands. Let T be the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of V = Ext^n_D(K,K) induced by phi. For u in V_{alpha,beta} = Ext^n_D(K_alpha,K_beta), viewed as a morphism K_alpha -> K_beta[n], functoriality of F^* and the isomorphisms phi_alpha, phi_beta give T(u) = phi_beta[n] compose F^*(u) compose phi_alpha^{-1}. This lies in Ext^n_D(K_alpha,K_beta). Therefore each V_{alpha,beta} is T-stable, and T is the direct sum of the restrictions T_{alpha,beta} = T restricted to V_{alpha,beta}. Since T is invertible and V_{alpha,beta} is finite-dimensional, each T_{alpha,beta} is invertible; equivalently, it is the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism induced by phi_alpha and phi_beta. This proves the phi-equivariant direct-sum decomposition. 4. Semisimplicity on a direct sum. We use the following elementary linear algebra fact over the algebraically closed field Qbar_l: if V = direct sum_{i=1}^m V_i is a finite direct sum of T-stable subspaces and T = direct sum T_i, then T is semisimple if and only if each T_i is semisimple. Since Qbar_l is algebraically closed, semisimple means diagonalizable. If T is diagonalizable, then V decomposes as a direct sum of eigenspaces E_lambda(T). The projection onto E_lambda(T) is a polynomial in T (because the minimal polynomial of T has distinct roots), hence it preserves each V_i. Therefore V_i = direct sum_lambda (V_i intersect E_lambda(T)), and T_i is diagonalizable. Conversely, if each T_i is diagonalizable, choose an eigenbasis of each V_i; the union of these bases is an eigenbasis of V, so T is diagonalizable. Applying this fact to V = Ext^n_D(K,K) and the stable summands V_{alpha,beta} = Ext^n_D(K_alpha,K_beta) gives that the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism induced by phi is semisimple on Ext^n_D(K,K) if and only if it is semisimple on every Ext^n_D(K_alpha,K_beta). This completes the proof.

lemma_20c.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, let l != p, and let D = D^b_c(Xbar,Q_l), where Xbar = X_{overline{F}_q}. Recall that a finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space V with an arithmetic Frobenius automorphism F is pure of weight w if every eigenvalue of F on V tensor_Q_l Q_l_bar has Weil absolute value q^{w/2}. Let P',P,P'',Q be perverse sheaves, viewed as objects of D, equipped with arithmetic Frobenius structures, and suppose 0 -> P' -> P -> P'' -> 0 is a Frobenius-equivariant short exact sequence in the heart of the perverse t-structure. Assume P',P,P'' are pure of weight a and Q is pure of weight b. If for every n >= 0 the induced Frobenius automorphism on Hom_D(P',Q[n]) and on Hom_D(P'',Q[n]) is pure of weight b-a+n, then for every n >= 0 the induced Frobenius automorphism on Hom_D(P,Q[n]) is pure of weight b-a+n. The analogous statement holds in the second variable: if 0 -> Q' -> Q -> Q'' -> 0 is a Frobenius-equivariant short exact sequence of perverse sheaves pure of weight b, P is pure of weight a, and Hom_D(P,Q'[n]) and Hom_D(P,Q''[n]) are pure of weight b-a+n for every n >= 0, then Hom_D(P,Q[n]) is pure of weight b-a+n for every n >= 0.
lemma_20c.proof:
Proof. We first record two elementary facts about finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces equipped with a Q_l-linear automorphism. Call such a space V pure of weight w if every eigenvalue of the automorphism on V tensor_Q_l Q_l_bar has Weil absolute value q^{w/2}. The zero space is pure of every weight vacuously.

(i) If V is pure of weight w and U is a stable subspace, then U and V/U are pure of weight w. Indeed, choose a basis of U and extend it to a basis of V. The matrix of the automorphism is block upper triangular, with diagonal blocks given by the induced automorphisms on U and V/U. Hence the characteristic polynomial of V is the product of the characteristic polynomials of U and V/U, so every eigenvalue of U or V/U is an eigenvalue of V.

(ii) If 0 -> U -> V -> W -> 0 is an exact sequence of stable subspaces and quotients, and U and W are pure of weight w, then V is pure of weight w. Again choose a basis adapted to U; the matrix of V is block upper triangular with diagonal blocks the matrices of U and W. Thus the eigenvalues of V are the union of the eigenvalues of U and W, all of which have Weil absolute value q^{w/2}.

Next, we justify finiteness and Frobenius-equivariance of the relevant Hom spaces. Since X is smooth projective, it is proper. The perverse sheaves P', P, P'', Q are objects of D = D^b_c(Xbar,Q_l) equipped with arithmetic Frobenius structures. For any two such objects A and B and any integer n, Hom_D(A,B[n]) = Ext^n_D(A,B). By lemma_16_frob_stable, this vector space is finite-dimensional over Q_l. The Frobenius structures on A and B induce a Q_l-linear automorphism on Hom_D(A,B[n]) by the usual formula u -> phi_B[n] o F_X^*(u) o phi_A^{-1}. If f:A -> B is a Frobenius-equivariant morphism, then precomposition and postcomposition with f commute with these induced automorphisms. The standard long exact sequence of Hom spaces attached to a distinguished triangle of Frobenius-equivariant objects is therefore a long exact sequence of Frobenius modules; in particular, all maps in it are Frobenius-equivariant.

First variable. The Frobenius-equivariant short exact sequence 0 -> P' -> P -> P'' -> 0 in the heart of the perverse t-structure gives a distinguished triangle P' -> P -> P'' -> P'[1] in D. Applying the contravariant cohomological functor Hom_D(-,Q[n]) yields, for each n >= 0, an exact sequence
A_n -> B_n -> C_n -> D_n,
where
A_n = Hom_D(P'',Q[n]),
B_n = Hom_D(P,Q[n]),
C_n = Hom_D(P',Q[n]),
D_n = Hom_D(P'',Q[n+1]).
Let w_n = b-a+n. By hypothesis, A_n and C_n are pure of weight w_n. The space D_n is also finite-dimensional and carries its induced Frobenius automorphism, but its purity is not needed for the argument.

Write the maps as
alpha_n:A_n -> B_n,
beta_n:B_n -> C_n,
delta_n:C_n -> D_n.
Because these maps are Frobenius-equivariant, their kernels and images are stable subspaces. Exactness gives
im(alpha_n) = ker(beta_n),
im(beta_n) = ker(delta_n).
Therefore beta_n induces an isomorphism of Frobenius modules
B_n/im(alpha_n) -> ker(delta_n),
and we have a short exact sequence of Frobenius modules
0 -> im(alpha_n) -> B_n -> ker(delta_n) -> 0.

Now im(alpha_n) is isomorphic to A_n/ker(alpha_n), a quotient of the pure space A_n of weight w_n. By fact (i), im(alpha_n) is pure of weight w_n. Also ker(delta_n) is a stable subspace of the pure space C_n of weight w_n. By fact (i), ker(delta_n) is pure of weight w_n. Finally, by fact (ii), the extension B_n of im(alpha_n) by ker(delta_n) is pure of weight w_n. Thus Hom_D(P,Q[n]) is pure of weight b-a+n for every n >= 0.

Second variable. The Frobenius-equivariant short exact sequence 0 -> Q' -> Q -> Q'' -> 0 gives a distinguished triangle Q' -> Q -> Q'' -> Q'[1]. Applying the covariant cohomological functor Hom_D(P,-[n]) gives, for each n >= 0, an exact sequence
A'_n -> B'_n -> C'_n -> D'_n,
where
A'_n = Hom_D(P,Q'[n]),
B'_n = Hom_D(P,Q[n]),
C'_n = Hom_D(P,Q''[n]),
D'_n = Hom_D(P,Q'[n+1]).
By hypothesis, A'_n and C'_n are pure of weight w_n = b-a+n. The same argument as above shows that im(A'_n -> B'_n) is a quotient of A'_n, hence pure of weight w_n, and ker(C'_n -> D'_n) is a subspace of C'_n, hence pure of weight w_n. Moreover, B'_n fits into a short exact sequence of Frobenius modules
0 -> im(A'_n -> B'_n) -> B'_n -> ker(C'_n -> D'_n) -> 0.
By fact (ii), B'_n = Hom_D(P,Q[n]) is pure of weight w_n = b-a+n. This proves the analogous statement in the second variable.

lemma_25.statement: Let l be a prime, let m >= 1, and let V_0,...,V_{m-1} be finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces. Let T: V = direct sum_{j=0}^{m-1} V_j -> V be a Q_l-linear automorphism such that T(V_j) = V_{j+1} for all j modulo m. Then T is semisimple on V if and only if T^m restricted to V_0 is semisimple on V_0.
lemma_25.proof:
Proof. If V_0=0, then T(V_0)=V_1 forces V_1=0, and inductively all V_j=0; the unique operator on the zero space is semisimple, so both assertions hold. Hence assume V_0 is nonzero. We use lemma_5: a Q_l-linear operator on a finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space is semisimple if and only if its extension to Q_l_bar is diagonalizable. Over an algebraically closed field, diagonalizable is equivalent to having square-free minimal polynomial: a diagonalizable operator has minimal polynomial product of distinct linear factors corresponding to its occurring eigenvalues, and conversely a square-free minimal polynomial splits into distinct linear factors and yields a direct-sum decomposition into eigenspaces.

First relate S:=T^m|_{V_0} to T^m on V. Indices are modulo m. Since T is an automorphism and T(V_j)=V_{j+1}, the restriction T^j:V_0 -> V_j is a Q_l-linear isomorphism for each j=0,...,m-1. Let S_j:=T^m|_{V_j}. Because T^m(V_j)=V_j, S_j is an automorphism of V_j. For v in V_0, T^j(Sv)=T^{j+m}v=S_j(T^jv), so T^j conjugates S to S_j. By lemma_8, S is semisimple on V_0 if and only if S_j is semisimple on V_j. The operator T^m on V=direct sum_{j=0}^{m-1} V_j is the direct sum of the S_j. By lemma_9, T^m is semisimple on V if and only if every S_j is semisimple. Combining these equivalences gives (1) S is semisimple on V_0 if and only if T^m is semisimple on V.

Next prove an auxiliary claim: if A is a Q_l-linear automorphism of a finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space W, then A is semisimple on W if and only if A^m is semisimple on W. The zero-dimensional case is trivial, so assume W nonzero. If A is semisimple, then by lemma_5 A is diagonalizable over Q_l_bar. In a basis of eigenvectors of A, the matrix of A^m is diagonal, so A^m is diagonalizable over Q_l_bar; lemma_5 gives that A^m is semisimple. Conversely, assume A^m is semisimple. By lemma_5, A^m is diagonalizable over Q_l_bar. Working over Q_l_bar, let f(x) be the minimal polynomial of A^m. Then f(x)=product_{r=1}^s (x-a_r) with pairwise distinct a_r. Since A is invertible, A^m is invertible, so 0 is not a root of f; hence every a_r is nonzero. The polynomial f(x^m) annihilates A because f(A^m)=0. Therefore the minimal polynomial mu_A(x) of A over Q_l_bar divides f(x^m). We claim f(x^m) is square-free. For fixed r, x^m-a_r has no repeated root: if beta is a root, then beta is nonzero, and its derivative m*beta^{m-1} is nonzero since Q_l_bar has characteristic 0. If r != r', the polynomials x^m-a_r and x^m-a_{r'} have no common root, since a common root beta would give beta^m=a_r=a_{r'}. Thus the factors x^m-a_r are pairwise coprime and separable, so f(x^m) has no repeated roots. Hence mu_A is square-free, so A is diagonalizable over Q_l_bar, and lemma_5 implies A is semisimple on W. This proves the auxiliary claim.

Apply the auxiliary claim to A=T and W=V. It yields that T is semisimple on V if and only if T^m is semisimple on V. Combining with equivalence (1) yields that T is semisimple on V if and only if S=T^m|_{V_0} is semisimple on V_0. This is the desired statement.

lemma_23.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, with ell != p, and let C_1,...,C_m be the geometric connected components of X_{\overline{F}_q}. There is a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism R\mathcal{H}om(IC_X,IC_X) \cong \bigoplus_{j=1}^m Q_{\ell,C_j}, where Q_{\ell,C_j} is the constant sheaf on C_j extended by zero to X_{\overline{F}_q}. In particular, R\mathcal{H}om(IC_X,IC_X) is a pure semisimple complex of weight 0 on X_{\overline{F}_q}.
lemma_23.proof:
Proof. Write Xbar = X_{Fbar_q} and let F denote arithmetic Frobenius x -> x^q. We work in the mixed derived category D^b_m(Xbar,Q_l); a complex is called semisimple if it is isomorphic to a direct sum of shifts of simple mixed perverse sheaves, and pure of weight 0 if all its perverse cohomology sheaves are pure of weight 0. If X is empty the assertion is trivial, so assume X nonempty.

Let X = disjoint union_{s=1}^r X_s be the decomposition into connected components over F_q. Each X_s is open and closed in X, hence smooth projective over F_q; let d_s = dim X_s and Y_s = (X_s)_{Fbar_q}. The geometric connected components C_1,...,C_m are partitioned by the sets O_s = pi_0(Y_s). These O_s are exactly the F_q-orbits on pi_0(Xbar). Indeed, Gal(Fbar_q/F_q) acts on pi_0(Xbar), and a connected component over F_q corresponds to a minimal Galois-stable subset of pi_0(Xbar), namely one orbit.

1. The canonical isomorphism. By Lemma_1 there is a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism IC_X isomorphic to direct sum_{C in pi_0(Xbar)} Q_l[dim C]. Grouping the summands over the F_q-components X_s gives an F-equivariant decomposition IC_X isomorphic to direct sum_{s=1}^r A_s, where A_s = Q_{l,Y_s}[d_s]. The supports Y_s are pairwise disjoint open-closed subsets of Xbar. Hence for s != t the internal Hom sheaf RHom(A_s,A_t) is zero, because a morphism between sheaves with disjoint supports is zero. Therefore RHom(IC_X,IC_X) is isomorphic to direct sum_{s=1}^r RHom(A_s,A_s). For each s, X_s is smooth projective of pure dimension d_s over F_q. Lemma_14 applied to X_s gives a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism RHom(Q_{l,Y_s}[d_s], Q_{l,Y_s}[d_s]) isomorphic to Q_{l,Y_s}. Since Y_s is the disjoint union of the geometric components in O_s, Q_{l,Y_s} is isomorphic to direct sum_{C in O_s} Q_{l,C}, where Q_{l,C} denotes the constant sheaf on C extended by zero to Xbar. Combining these identifications yields the required canonical F-equivariant isomorphism RHom(IC_X,IC_X) isomorphic to direct sum_{j=1}^m Q_{l,C_j}. Here the RHS is given the natural F-action which sends Q_{l,C_j} to Q_{l,F(C_j)} by pullback of constant sheaves.

2. Purity. For each s, X_s is smooth projective over F_q, so Lemma_12 applied to X_s says that Q_{l,Y_s}, with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure, is pure of weight 0. Finite direct sums of pure weight 0 objects are pure of weight 0, because the weight filtration of a direct sum is the direct sum of the weight filtrations. Hence direct sum_s Q_{l,Y_s}, and therefore RHom(IC_X,IC_X), is pure of weight 0.

3. Semisimplicity as a mixed complex. The decomposition into individual C_j is only a geometric decomposition; the mixed semisimple decomposition is obtained by grouping into the F-orbits O_s. Set P_s = Q_{l,Y_s}[d_s]. By Lemma_19 applied to X_s, P_s = IC_{X_s} is a pure perverse sheaf of weight 0. We prove that P_s is simple in the abelian category of F-equivariant perverse sheaves on Xbar.

First we note that each geometric summand P_C = Q_{l,C}[d_s] is simple as a perverse sheaf. Fix C. Choose a finite extension k/F_q over which C is defined and geometrically connected, for instance the fixed field of the stabilizer of C in Gal(Fbar_q/F_q). Lemma_1 applied to C/k says that IC_C is semisimple and canonically isomorphic to Q_{l,C}[dim C]. Lemma_14 applied to C/k gives RHom(Q_{l,C}[dim C], Q_{l,C}[dim C]) isomorphic to Q_{l,C}; taking H^0 yields End(Q_{l,C}[dim C]) isomorphic to H^0(C,Q_l) = Q_l, because C is connected. A semisimple object whose endomorphism algebra is a division algebra is simple: if it decomposed as a direct sum of simples with more than one summand, or with multiplicity greater than one, its endomorphism algebra would contain a nontrivial idempotent or a matrix algebra M_n(D) with n > 1. Hence P_C is simple. Each P_C is regarded as a perverse sheaf on Xbar by extension by zero from the open-closed subset C; this preserves simplicity. The P_C for distinct C have disjoint supports, so they are pairwise non-isomorphic.

Now P_s is isomorphic to direct sum_{C in O_s} P_C. Forgetting the Frobenius structure is exact and faithful, and this is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic simple perverse sheaves. Let M be a subobject of P_s in the mixed perverse category. Its underlying perverse sheaf is a subobject of the semisimple object P_s, hence is a direct sum of a subset S of the simple constituents P_C. The Frobenius structure on M forces S to be invariant under the action of F on the constituents. By Lemma_1 the F-structure on IC_X, and hence on P_s, permutes the P_C according to the action of F on O_s; by construction O_s is a single F-orbit. Therefore the only F-invariant subsets are the empty set and O_s itself. Thus M = 0 or M = P_s, so P_s is simple, and in particular semisimple, as a mixed perverse sheaf. Equivalently, the F-equivariant endomorphism algebra is the invariant part of direct sum_{C in O_s} End(P_C) isomorphic to Q_l^{O_s}, namely Q_l.

Since P_s is simple and pure of weight 0, the complex Q_{l,Y_s} = P_s[-d_s] is a semisimple mixed complex of weight 0: its only nonzero perverse cohomology sheaf is ^pH^{-d_s}(Q_{l,Y_s}) = P_s, which is simple and pure of weight 0 (Lemma_11 also shows that Q_{l,Y_s}[d_s] is perverse). A finite direct sum of such complexes is again a finite direct sum of shifts of simple pure weight 0 perverse sheaves, hence is a pure semisimple complex of weight 0. Therefore direct sum_{s=1}^r Q_{l,Y_s}, equivalently direct sum_{j=1}^m Q_{l,C_j}, is pure semisimple of weight 0 in the mixed category. By the canonical F-equivariant isomorphism proved in part 1, RHom(IC_X,IC_X) is pure semisimple of weight 0. QED.

lemma_24.statement: Let X be a proper variety over F_q, let ell != p, and let K be a pure semisimple perverse sheaf on X_bar = X_{overline F_q} with an arithmetic Frobenius structure. After extending scalars to Q_l_bar, decompose K into the finitely many Frobenius-orbit isotypic components K = direct sum_alpha K_alpha. For an orbit of length d_alpha, choose a simple constituent L_{alpha,0}, let L_{alpha,j} be its j-th arithmetic Frobenius translate, and let M_alpha be the multiplicity space, so that K_alpha = direct sum_{j=0}^{d_alpha-1} L_{alpha,j} tensor M_alpha. For every integer n, put V^n = H^n(X_bar,K) tensor Q_l_bar and, for each alpha, V_{alpha,j}^n = H^n(X_bar,L_{alpha,j}) tensor M_alpha. The induced arithmetic Frobenius automorphism F on V^n maps V_{alpha,j}^n isomorphically to V_{alpha,j+1}^n, with indices taken modulo d_alpha. Let F_alpha^{d_alpha} be the automorphism of V_{alpha,0}^n obtained by restricting F^{d_alpha} to V_{alpha,0}^n. Then F is semisimple on V^n if and only if, for every alpha, F_alpha^{d_alpha} is semisimple on V_{alpha,0}^n.
lemma_24.proof:
Proof. Let D = D^b_c(Xbar, Q_l). We first record finite-dimensionality and the correct Ext convention. The constant sheaf Q_l on Xbar has a canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure, namely the identity isomorphism F_X^*Q_l = Q_l, and K is assumed to be equipped with an arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism phi_K:F_X^*K -> K. By lemma_16_frob_stable, Ext^i_D(Q_l,K) is finite-dimensional over Q_l for every integer i. With the usual convention Ext^i_D(A,B) = Hom_D(A,B[i]), we have H^n(Xbar,K) = Hom_D(Q_l,K[n]) = Ext^n_D(Q_l,K); this is Ext^n, not Ext^{-n}. Hence H^n(Xbar,K) is finite-dimensional, and V^n = H^n(Xbar,K) tensor_Q_l Q_lbar is finite-dimensional over Q_lbar. The pair (phi_Q,phi_K) induces a Q_l-linear automorphism F on H^n(Xbar,K): for f:Q_l -> K[n], F(f) = phi_K[n] o F_X^*(f) o phi_Q^{-1}. We extend F Q_lbar-linearly to V^n.

By the decomposition stated in the lemma, after extending scalars to Q_lbar we have K = direct_sum_alpha K_alpha, with K_alpha = direct_sum_{j=0}^{d_alpha-1} L_{alpha,j} tensor M_alpha, and the Frobenius structure permutes the orbit summands. Since H^n is additive on finite direct sums and L_{alpha,j} tensor M_alpha is a finite direct sum of copies of L_{alpha,j}, we obtain a canonical decomposition V^n = direct_sum_alpha W_alpha^n, where W_alpha^n = direct_sum_{j=0}^{d_alpha-1} V_{alpha,j}^n, and V_{alpha,j}^n = H^n(Xbar,L_{alpha,j}) tensor M_alpha. Each V_{alpha,j}^n is finite-dimensional because it is a direct summand of the finite-dimensional space V^n.
